items.author: Andrej Karpathy
items.bio: I like training large deep neural nets.
items.summary_en:
We're starting to leave the territory where you'd test an LLM by e.g. "create an svg of pelican on a bicycle". As one idea to generalize it, I was interested what Opus 5 would do if I gave it the first paragraph of the Lord of the Rings, a 1M token budget (~$10) and asked for three js render of it. Opus went off for ~2 hours and wrote 5500 lines of code that (procedurally) rendered the story. It's kind of janky but fun. But it's a bit mindboggling that the LLM has to place and orchestrate various polygon assets in (x,y,z) coordinates and write code that animates it all, and that it even does anything at all.

I also like this kind of examples because no one in their right mind would ever spend the time to write something this custom but LLMs have all the stamina and patience in the world, so it's an example where we go from "no one would ever do this" to "sure, why not, it's ~free". There might be a lot more. But I'm excited about creating hyper custom worlds that you can imagine dropping players into, e.g. here to participate in the LoTR story as a spectator NPC, or one of the characters, or etc. Something like an ephemeral GTA of X on demand.

Last thought is that the domain of worlds/games exposes a weakness in LLMs: they can't easily audit their work because they aren't able to efficiently and natively perceive videos or play games within them. Here, Opus 5 had to very slowly and painstakingly take screenshots at different points, and it messed up a few times and created a bunch of jank. An example of raw capability (multimodal, gameplay) that I think is still quite lacking.
items.summary_zh:
LLM 测试已经不该停留在“画个骑自行车的鹈鹕”这种玩具题了：给 Opus 5 一段《魔戒》开头、100 万 token 和 10 美元，它能熬两小时写出 5500 行 Three.js，把故事硬生生程序化渲染出来。

真正的变化是，过去没人会手写这种一次性定制世界，现在模型有无限耐心，“没人会做”正在变成“为什么不做，反正近乎免费”；但游戏/世界也暴露了硬伤：模型还不能原生高效看视频、玩游戏、审自己的作品，所以能力很野，质量很糙。

items.author: Aaron Levie
items.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
items.summary_en:
We’re going to see an increasing divergence between what AI does in our personal lives and in daily productivity vs. what it can do in very deep domains like math, science, legal, coding and more.

Up to some threshold, capability was evenly felt across all domains because the models were just becoming mildly useful in general. Now, the deep domain work is about to go vertical. 

Most people won’t actually notice these benefits in their day to day life directly (indirectly they certainly will over time), but the experts in these fields will. And there’s no inherent ceiling to what capabilities are needed, unlike in the consumer space where needs can get met relatively straightforwardly.

This will often lead to a capability overhang, though, as many of these performance gains need to be applied to data sets and workflows in an applied way for that area of work. But this is ultimately how you get breakthroughs in life sciences, real world automation, new cyber capabilities, and more.
items.summary_zh: AI 在日常生活里的提升会越来越不显眼，但在数学、科学、法律、编程等深水区会开始垂直爆发。真正的红利不在消费端小修小补，而在专家把能力接进数据集和工作流后，撬出生命科学、现实自动化、网络能力等硬突破。

items.author: No Priors
items.title: Building an Autonomous Enterprise for Real-World Services with Netic Founder Melisa Tokmak
items.summary_en:
Speaker 1 | 00:05 - 00:30
Today on our priors, we're joined by Melissa Tachmak. Melissa is the founder and CEO of Netic, a company that builds AI for different real world services like HVAC, pet care, a variety of other things like that, roofers. Prior to Netic, Melissa was a director of engineering and worked on various aspects of go to market for Scale dot AI and, also has experiences from Meta. Welcome to No Prize, Melissa. Melissa, thanks for joining us today at No Prize.

Speaker 2 | 00:30 - 00:31
Thank you for having me.

Speaker 1 | 00:31 - 00:45
Yeah. Maybe we can start off by talking a little bit about your business and what you're building because I think that, you're doing something really interesting in the real world, and you're kind of marrying AI in the real world. So could you tell us more about your company and Netic and, you know, what you're focused on?

Speaker 2 | 00:45 - 01:00
Yeah. Netic builds AI to run millions of real world businesses that keep the world running. That means, basically, we work with large enterprises in essential services. We started in essential services.

Speaker 1 | 01:00 - 01:02
What be an example of essential service?

Speaker 2 | 01:02 - 02:02
Imagine a billion dollar revenue home services companies in HVAC, plumbing, electric, or consumer wellness companies, like, where you can become a member and really go do a lot of sports or different activities, hospitality, automotive, pet services, across the board. So every single thing that you need to run your life or that you want to do are a good example. And a lot of these businesses are actually quite large businesses, and they interact with millions of end users themselves, usually that are consumers or businesses themselves. So Netic exists between the company and its cust
items.summary_zh: Netic 要做的不是给互联网产品添个 AI 按钮，而是让 AI 直接接管那些维持现实世界运转的企业：暖通、管道、电工、宠物服务、酒店、汽车、健身与消费健康。它盯上的是真正有规模、每天和数百万用户打交道的线下服务公司。
